title: El Trapiche de Cuautla, VISTA
comment: trapiche-cuautla (VISTA): época, hacia 1910 (ropa de época, sin uniformes). Portal de arcos de piedra de una hacienda cañera de Morelos, de tarde. Caras comunes, no famosas; los tres se distinguen a simple vista.

chars.FIDELINA_VILLASENOR: Mexican woman, the widowed owner of a sugarcane hacienda around 1910, 48 years old, light-brown skin, black hair with a few grey strands pulled into a tight bun with a tortoiseshell comb, proud dark eyes, a high-collared black lace blouse with long sleeves, a long dark-grey skirt, an ivory cameo brooch at the collar, period clothing, her hands empty.
chars.ADALBERTO_LARREA: Mexican man, the powerful neighboring hacienda owner around 1910, 62 years old, fair tanned skin, a neat grey goatee and grey hair, heavy eyelids, a white linen three-piece suit with a gold watch chain, a white straw panama hat, period clothing, his hands empty.
chars.ELIAS_CERVERA: Mexican mestizo man, a hacienda administrator around 1910, 34 years old, brown skin, wavy black hair, a thin black mustache, calm intense eyes, a cream cotton shirt with rolled sleeves, a brown wool vest, dark trousers, a wide-brimmed straw hat, period clothing, his hands empty.

locs.LOC_TRAPICHECUAUTLA: Covered stone arcade of the main house of an old sugarcane hacienda in Morelos around 1910, in the warm afternoon: thick stone arches, terracotta tile floor, a long table with a white tablecloth, a glass jug of agua fresca and glasses, potted ferns, beyond the arches green sugarcane fields, an old stone aqueduct and a tall brick mill chimney, no readable text, no signs, no logos, no people.
